sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes
Requested: Decrease minPoolCost from 170 ada to 75 ada and increase Plutus memory limits to complete a two-step cumulative 25% increase.
Stated amount: not stated in document
Deliverables: minPoolCost changed to 75,000,000 Lovelace, maxTxExecutionUnits[memory] changed from 16,500,000 to 17,500,000, maxBlockExecutionUnits[memory] changed from 72,000,000 to 77,500,000
Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The action bundles two otherwise unrelated parameter changes for submission efficiency and to allow SPO input on minPoolCost.
Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): minPoolCost would be reduced from 170,000,000 Lovelace to 75,000,000 Lovelace, a decrease of about 55.9%.

Claim (economic, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The proposer says declining reserve-funded block rewards have increased the delegator penalty on single-block pools from about 28.3% after the 2023 change to about 52.8%, with a projection of 100% around epoch 758 in February 2028 if unaddressed.
Claim (economic, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The proposer says lowering minPoolCost should improve competitiveness for small pools but would not force any SPO to reduce its fee.

Claim (technical, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The proposer says IO Research's updated incentives report concludes that a high fixed-fee floor may favor Sybil-style stake fragmentation by large operators and recommends lowering minPoolCost toward zero, ideally paired with minPoolMargin.

Claim (economic, proposer_asserted, medium materiality): The proposer says two years of post-2023 data show the market did not collapse toward the 170 ada floor, with 340 ada remaining dominant and smaller competitively positioned pools adopting the lower floor.
